verses.1: Those great-souled kings departed joyfully, shaking the earth with their throngs of thousands of elephants and horses.
verses.2: Many Akshauhinis, with their delighted forces and vehicles, were indeed present there, prepared for Rama's cause by Bharata's command.
verses.3: And those kings, filled with the pride of their strength, said that they did not see Rama and Ravana standing before them in battle.
verses.4: They felt that they had been brought uselessly by Bharata, as the Rakshasas would have certainly been quickly killed by the kings themselves.
verses.5: Protected by the strength of Rama's and Lakshmana's arms, they would have happily fought on the other side of the ocean, free from any anxiety.
verses.6: These and many other stories, thousands of them, were narrated by the kings there as they returned to their own kingdoms, filled with joy.
verses.7: Their own excellent and prosperous kingdoms were joyful, full of abundant wealth and grain, and rich in resources.
verses.8: The kings, having returned to their respective cities, then brought various jewels and gifts to please Rama.
verses.9: They presented horses, vehicles, jewels, rutting elephants, excellent sandalwoods, and divine ornaments.
verses.10: They also offered gems, pearls, corals, beautiful female servants, various goats and sheep, and diverse chariots.
verses.11: Bharata, Lakshmana, and the mighty Shatrughna, having received those treasures, then returned to their own city.
verses.12: Having arrived back in the beautiful city of Ayodhya, those best among men presented the various wonderful jewels to Rama.
verses.13: The great-souled Rama, filled with joy, received all those gifts and then gave them to King Sugriva, who had accomplished great deeds.
verses.14: Rama similarly gave gifts to Vibhishana and also to the other Rakshasas and Vanaras by whom he was surrounded and with whose help he had achieved victory.
verses.15: All those mighty Vanaras and Rakshasas wore the jewels given by Rama on their heads and arms.
verses.16: The valiant King of the Ikshvakus, the great warrior Rama, placed Hanuman and the mighty-armed Angada on his lap.
verses.17: Rama, whose eyes resembled lotus petals, spoke to Sugriva, saying that Angada was his good son and Hanuman was also his minister.
verses.18: O lord of monkeys, Angada and Hanuman, being engaged in your counsel and devoted to my welfare, indeed deserve various honors for your sake.
verses.19: Having spoken thus, the greatly renowned Rama then removed valuable ornaments from his own body and fastened them upon Angada and Hanuman.
verses.20: And Rama then addressed the very powerful best of the troop leaders: Nila, Nala, Kesarin, Kumuda, and Gandhamadana.
verses.21: He also addressed Sushena, Panasa, the brave Mainda, Dvivida, Jambavan, Gavaksha, Vinata, and Dhumra.
verses.22: This verse lists the names of several prominent monkey chiefs: Valimukha, Prajangha, the mighty Sannada, Darimukha, Dadhimukha, and Indrajānu, who were all leaders of troops.
verses.23: Speaking sweetly and gently, as if drinking them in with his eyes, Rama declared that they were his friends, his very body, and his brothers.
verses.24: Rama declared that he, a dweller of the forest, was rescued from distress by them, and King Sugriva was blessed to have them, the best among friends.
verses.25: Having spoken thus, Rama, the best among men, gave them ornaments and very valuable diamonds as was fitting, and also embraced them.
verses.26: The monkeys, tawny like honey, drank fragrant honey and ate well-prepared meats, roots, and fruits.
verses.27: While they were thus dwelling, more than a month passed, yet all of them perceived it as merely a moment due to their profound devotion to Rama.
verses.28: Rama also delighted in the company of those form-changing monkeys, the greatly valorous Rakshasas, and the exceedingly strong bears.
verses.29: Thus, for all those greatly delighted monkeys and Rakshasas, the second pleasant month passed happily.
verses.30: While they were experiencing supreme joy in the beautiful city of Ikshvaku, time passed happily for them due to Rama's delightful actions. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 39 ।। Thus ends the thirty-ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
